analysis.title: US Economic Weekly: Oct FOMC preview: Sea change or wee change?
key_insights: BofA keeps its call for a 25bp Fed hike at the Oct 28 FOMC but admits it would be a heavy lift given this week's price action. Conviction that the Fed should hike is strong, conviction that it will is low.

The large, broad-based beat in Sep inflation more than offsets last month's downward revisions. Core PCE could plausibly end 2026 at 3.4% y/y, and the booming nominal economy raises the risk that the energy shock gets passed through.

The long end is no longer doing the Fed's tightening. The 10y yield has nearly fallen back below 5% and the 10y term premium is down over 25bp. BofA says a Fed that cited higher yields as a reason for caution but ignores their fall would show an asymmetric reaction function.

Staying on hold would keep the Fed's option of being one and done, which makes sense only if it judged the Sep hike a mistake. Hiking keeps open a Dec hike on the same cadence as the 2024 and 2025 cuts. BofA thinks the Dec option is more valuable given most of the FOMC already backs two hikes this year.

Williams and Jefferson spoke before the Sep data and their forward guidance led markets to price out the Oct hike. BofA says this cannot be squared with Chair Warsh's stated objection to forward guidance. A hike would signal the Fed has exited coordinated messaging, while a hold risks leaving the policy path to markets or other FOMC members.

Markets price about a 10% chance of an Oct hike and roughly three more hikes at a quarterly cadence. Long-end yields are not questioning Fed credibility. BofA notes that under Powell or Yellen a hawkish surprise this large, six days before the midterms, would have had basically zero chance.

If the Fed hikes, BofA expects no substantive statement changes. If it holds, the sentence saying today's policy action will support a timelier return to the 2 percent goal would need to be omitted or edited.

Press conference scenario 1 (hike): Warsh would stress that inflation is too high and broad, financial conditions are not restrictive enough, activity is robust and the labor market stable. The challenge is not sounding too hawkish. Without forward guidance such as calling it a midcycle adjustment of no more than 75-100bp in total, markets could price over-tightening, causing a large risk-asset correction and twist-flattening of the curve.

Press conference scenario 2 (hold): Warsh would be pressed on how a hold squares with his comment that inflation is a choice, and on whether he endorsed Williams and Jefferson's guidance. The risk is a repeat of the July presser: twist-steepening of the curve, a weaker dollar and a moderate risk-asset selloff.

BofA's outlook does not change materially if the Fed holds in Oct. It would still expect hikes in Dec 2026 and Mar 2027, with risk skewed toward further hikes in Jun 2027 and perhaps Sep 2027 if y/y inflation stays sticky in 1H 2027 despite favorable base effects.

Sep PCE is expected to run hot after upside surprises in CPI, PPI and import prices, with both core goods and core services accelerating. BofA forecasts core PCE at +0.3% m/m (0.35% unrounded) and 3.1% y/y, and says the Fed may need to keep rates higher for longer.

BofA forecasts 3Q GDP at an above-consensus 3.5% q/q saar, with consumer spending up 3.5% and business investment led by equipment and IPP as AI-related capex keeps beating expectations. Its mechanical 3Q GDP tracking estimate rose one tenth to 3.7% after stronger Sep industrial production.

Next week's calendar: FOMC decision Wed Oct 28 at 2:00 pm and press conference at 2:30 pm, Sep PCE and the first 3Q GDP print Thu Oct 29, Q3 Employment Cost Index Fri Oct 30. The Fed blackout ends Thursday night, with Daly and Musalem scheduled to speak Friday.

Fed speak is split. Logan sees the range needing 50bp or more of additional hikes and Waller floated 75bp total at every other meeting. Collins, Williams, Musalem, Hammack and Goolsbee lean toward more tightening, while Bowman says she feels no urgency for further action. FOMC minutes said most participants saw another increase as likely appropriate by year end.
Bank of America card spending per household rose 4.9% y/y in the week ending Oct 17, and gas spending ran about +25.8% y/y. Furniture, department stores and entertainment were negative.

BofA core views: 2026 growth of 2.6% 4Q/4Q and 2.1% in 2027, job growth averaging 70k/mo in 2026 and around 60k in 2027 and 2028 with the unemployment rate at 4.1% through 2027, and core PCE finishing 2026 slightly above 3%. Underlying inflation is put at 2.5%, with inflation risks skewed to the upside.

BofA rates forecasts: Fed funds 4.25-4.50% by Dec 2026 and unchanged through 2027, 10-year Treasury 5.00% in Dec 2026 falling to 4.75% by Dec 2027, 2-year at 5.00% in Dec 2026. Dollar forecasts: EUR-USD 1.15 in Dec 2026 rising to 1.20, USD-JPY 152 falling to 145.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Energy pass-through keeps headline inflation well above core.

macro_indicators.reading: Large, broad-based upside surprise, magnitude not stated in text

macro_indicators.indicator: 10-year Treasury yield and ACM term premium
macro_indicators.reading: 10y nearly back below 5%, term premium down over 25bp
macro_indicators.interpretation: The bond rally removes the argument that higher long-end yields are doing the Fed's tightening.
Layoffs remain low, consistent with BofA's view of a stable labor market.
A sharp miss in housing, consistent with high mortgage rates weighing on interest-sensitive sectors.
Implies hikes in Oct and Dec, with the Fed then on hold through 2027.

risk_factors: Over-tightening fears if the Fed hikes without forward guidance, leading to a risk-asset correction and curve flattening.
Loss of Fed inflation-fighting credibility if the Fed holds after the hot Sep inflation data.
Energy shock pass-through into core inflation, with BofA's inflation risks skewed to the upside.
Mixed FOMC messaging, with Williams, Jefferson and other members moving market pricing independently of Chair Warsh.
Sticky y/y inflation in 1H 2027 despite favorable base effects could force hikes in Jun 2027 and perhaps Sep 2027.
Wobble in risk assets and a falling term premium could be used by the Fed to justify a slower pace.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots core PCE y/y with projections through end-2026 across a range of Oct-Dec monthly prints, showing a plausible 3.4% year-end level, assuming Sep core PCE of 0.35% m/m.
Exhibit 2 plots the ACM 10-year term premium, which has dropped over 25bp recently.
Exhibit 3 shows Fed hike pricing by meeting in bp, roughly consistent with three more hikes at a quarterly cadence.
vol_and_positioning: Market pricing is roughly consistent with three more Fed hikes at a quarterly cadence, with only about a 10% chance priced for Oct.

A hike without forward guidance could trigger a policy-error trade with a large risk-asset correction and twist-flattening of the curve. A hold could trigger a credibility trade with twist-steepening, a weaker dollar and a moderate risk selloff, as at the July presser.
geopolitical: The Iran war and tariffs are cited as the source of much of the current inflation overshoot, and the resulting energy shock is a risk to inflation pass-through.
US midterm elections fall six days after the Oct 28 FOMC decision, which BofA says would have deterred a hawkish surprise under earlier Fed chairs.

tension_points.bull_case: A hike is warranted. The Sep inflation beat was large and broad, core PCE could end 2026 at 3.4%, financial conditions are not restrictive enough, and the bond rally means long yields no longer do the Fed's work. A hike keeps the Dec option open and signals the Fed has exited coordinated messaging.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets price only about a 10% chance of a hike and recent price action makes it a heavy lift. A hike six days before the midterms could trigger an over-tightening trade, while Bowman sees no urgency and some officials favor a quarterly cadence.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Staying on hold would make sense only if the Fed concluded the Sep hike was a policy mistake. BofA's multi-hike outlook would otherwise be unchanged by a hold.

tension_points.bull_case: If the Fed hikes, Warsh has an easier presser by stressing that inflation is too high and broad, activity is robust and the labor market stable. Forward guidance such as calling it a midcycle adjustment of 75-100bp in total could cap tightening in financial conditions.
tension_points.bear_case: A hike with no guidance risks an over-tightening policy-error trade, a large risk-asset correction and twist-flattening. A hold risks a credibility trade like the July presser, with twist-steepening, a weaker dollar and a moderate risk selloff.

theme_stances.key_argument: Inflation is too high and broad, and the bond rally means long yields are no longer tightening for the Fed, so it should hike in Oct even though markets price only a small chance.
theme_stances.evidence: A strong case to hike, a heavy lift to deliver

theme_stances.evidence: AI-related capex continues to exceed expectations
